title: Control engineering changes and recover prior states
statement: Project decision owners, engineers and maintainers need to resume controlled engineering work from a current structured handoff, understand important decisions and completed outcomes, and recover explicitly retained engineering states and operational information without depending on the originating conversation.

what.problem: Interrupted work can lose its goal, authority, current progress and decision basis. Exhaustive activity recording adds effort without necessarily helping the next participant decide. Loss of local operational state also requires an explicit bounded recovery contract.
what.desired_outcome: Another authorized participant can identify the next sound engineering action from current context. Important rationale and compact completion accounts remain understandable; older operational detail is retained only while it has decision value or an explicit preservation obligation.

why.rationale: Continuity requires useful current information, not reconstruction of every action. Engineering Baselines and explicitly retained backups remain recoverable within their declared scope; disposable working evidence does not become a permanent archive obligation.

stakeholders: Engineering agents acting within project authority

conditions: Applies when changes are proposed, assessed, adopted, corrected, or retired, and when a retained baseline is inspected or recovered. It also applies when in-progress work is interrupted, resumed, or handed to another participant.

Keep active obligations, unresolved findings, important rationale and evidence needed for current reliance until explicitly resolved or coherently replaced. Working summaries and routine outputs may be replaced without historical copies. Retained engineering Baselines follow their separate preservation policy.

Also applies when creating an operational backup, restoring after loss or interruption, transferring retained work to another local environment, or migrating its storage representation. Backup and transfer do not renew assessments or authorize engineering actions.

contexts: Across Changes, Baselines, configuration management, and provenance in the governed engineering environment.

The selected project operational store, retained evidence artifacts, and explicitly selected backup or restoration destination, initially for one local checkout and one user with one or more local agents.

how.approach: Maintain one current handoff with goal/authority, governing basis, progress, open issues, relevant evidence, review standing and next action. Reference current engineering definitions at their owners. Record at meaningful handoffs or material decision changes, not every edit or test run. Preserve compact completed outcomes and selected decision-relevant detail. Recover retained Baselines and coherent operational backups within their declared scope without inventing unavailable work or renewing approval. IR-001 owns current definitions and applicable rationale; IR-008 owns reliable command access.

how_much.scope: One checkout and one user with one or more local agents. Current handoff and selective supporting detail, not event sourcing or a complete activity history. Completed Changes are historical statements, not live monitors of the repository; new regressions become linked new work. Explicit engineering Baseline retention and supported backup/restore remain distinct obligations. No guaranteed recovery of discarded, unsaved or unbacked-up information; no hosted synchronization or automatic merging.
limits: Zero loss or alteration of the selected baseline's recorded authoritative content, identities, relationships, and provenance in a recovery declared complete. This bound is relative to that baseline, not to later unrecorded work.

A restoration declared complete preserves the selected backup scope, record and subject identities, relationships, original decisions, assessment meaning and required retained artifact content. This claim does not include later unrecorded or unbacked-up work.

assumptions: Engineering Baseline recovery requires an intact retained Baseline and applicable interpretation rules. Operational restoration requires an accessible valid backup containing the declared records and retained artifact scope; the original operational store need not survive.
The user or selected backup arrangement keeps a usable copy outside the failure scope against which recovery is expected; no hosted storage service is supplied by this requirement.
constraints: Backup, import and restoration preserve historical meaning and do not grant fresh approval, evidence applicability or action authority.
Retirement and migration must resolve current dependencies and preserve required originals; a new storage representation does not authorize deletion of the only usable evidence.

sources.basis: Controlled transitions, identifiable baselines, recoverable states, and historical integrity.
